newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shares end below 800, led by blue chip sales.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shares end below 800, led by blue chip sales.

text.p: Large caps and blue chip shares dragged the stock index below the 800 point support level on Friday, as investors sat sidelined, uncertain about the future market direction, brokers said.
Worries that a hoped-for interest rate cut would be delayed also added to the gloom, they added.
The composite index fell 10.66 points to provisionally close at 793.78. Decliners beat advancers 538 to 351, while 26.72 million shares changed hands.
"It's a difficult market to read these days, because there is little direction," said Ha Yong-hyun of Hyundai Securities.

Despite a central bank announcement on Thursday it would cut the reserve requirement ratio for banks next month to an average of 5.5 percent, brokers said there was still worries interest rates would rise due to the huge number of bond issues seen in November.
About 3.1 trillion won worth of new corporate bond issues are expected. Three-year corporate bonds, as of Thursday, stood at 12.12 percent.
KEPCO fell 1,200 won to 24,800 won. Samsung Electronics fell 500 won to 63,000.
Among the only sectors that saw significant gains were pharmaceutical stocks and paper product shares.
Pharmaceutical shares are seen as having good earnings prospects. Choong Wae Pharmaceuticals gained 2,200 won to 40,200 in active trading.
South Korean paper companies, many of which have large pulp stockpiles, are expected to benefit from a rise in international pulp prices. Shinho Paper rose 440 won to 7,930.
The December futures contract ended down 0.8 of a point to 84.05, while the KOSPI 200 index lost 1.18 points to 82.93.
